problem: Frontier-based exploration is a heuristic on 2D grid maps that is hard to turn into an RL reward and cannot handle free 3D movement (e.g. stairs, multiple floors). Learned exploration rewards (curiosity, novelty, coverage, reconstruction) are not clearly better than frontier and mostly rely on 2D grid-map inputs.
motivation: Visual exploration underlies ObjectNav, EQA and rearrangement, so a general exploration reward that does not depend on a 2D map would transfer to many embodied tasks and to 3D-moving robots. The observation is that projecting the accumulated back-projected point cloud into a candidate view leaves holes exactly where nothing has been observed, so the number of missing pixels measures potential new information.
key_idea: Reward an action by the number of pixels that cannot be predicted when the accumulated depth point cloud is re-projected (view synthesis) into the view after that action, and add a topological-graph back-end to avoid revisiting states.
insight: Geometry-based novelty from view synthesis works as an exploration signal without any 2D map, and it needs a longer horizon to compete: online H=1 gives Area 0.40, H=5 gives 0.59, and the RL policy gives 0.62. The graph back-end matters: removing it drops Ours RL from 0.62/0.60/0.47 to 0.48/0.44/0.37 (Area/Obj/Lmk), because the agent gets stuck without a collision sensor. In ObjectNav, exploration plus a detector and point-goal navigation beats task-specific DD-PPO, and online search beats RL when accurate inputs are available.
method: View-synthesis image prediction: back-project the depth image with pose T_t and intrinsics K into a point cloud Q_t, accumulate Q_{0:t}, and project it to the predicted pose to get a predicted depth image. It is implemented as GPU tensor ops with max-pooling on inverse depth to fill quantization gaps.

Online reward: the reward of an action is the count of missing pixels in the predicted depth image. It is optimized over a horizon H by exhaustive search over discrete action sequences with weights w_h=1, and the reward is zeroed if more than 1/10 of the image is too-close points. Collisions are penalized via point-cloud overlap with the predicted robot pose, and the valid depth is 0.5–3.0 m.

RL reward: reward is proportional to the number of pixels that were missing in the predicted depth and become valid in the actual observation. The policy is ResNet-50 + LSTM(512) on a 256x256 depth image, pose (x,y,θ) and previous action, trained with PPO on HM3D for 340k updates.

Back-end topological graph search: nodes and edges are created for each possible action from the current pose. The path is chosen by reward divided by path length (for RL, the policy's action probability serves as the reward). Reached nodes are merged when the pose is close to an existing node, which prevents repeated visits.

ObjectNav pipeline: run Scaled-YOLOv4 (confidence 0.7) during exploration and, once the target is detected, switch to point-goal navigation using the same graph search with a Euclidean-distance-to-goal reward.

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 + LSTM policy (RL variant, trained from scratch with PPO); online variant is geometric search with no learning; Scaled-YOLOv4 (pretrained) for detection
setting.training_data: RL policy trained with PPO on the HM3D train split (340,000 updates) using the proposed reward; online variants are training-free; YOLO is a pretrained detector
setting.observation: Depth image (plus RGB for detection in ObjectNav) and relative pose x,y,θ; no 2D grid map and no bump sensor
setting.action_space: discrete: move forward, turn left/right (exploration); ObjectNav adds stop, tilt up, tilt down
setting.simulator: Habitat-Sim (MP3D for exploration, HM3D for Habitat Challenge 2022 ObjectNav)
setting.privileged: Ground-truth pose and noise-free depth from the simulator; for exploration metrics, MP3D object/landmark annotations are used only for evaluation

numbers.backbone: online view-synthesis search + Scaled-YOLOv4 + graph search

results: Exploration reward matches state-of-the-art learned exploration without 2D maps: Ours RL reaches Area/Obj/Lmk 0.62/0.60/0.47 versus frontier 0.64/0.57/0.50 and novelty 0.63/0.62/0.35. On Habitat Challenge 2022 ObjectNav test-standard, Ours (H=4) gets SR 0.33/SPL 0.18 versus DDPPO's 0.26/0.12.
limitations: Online optimization cost grows exponentially with horizon (H=5 did not finish within the 48h challenge limit), and RL performance is not yet sufficient to remove this cost.
Assumes an RGB-D camera and noise-free pose/depth in simulation, so it is untested with sensor noise, outdoors or on real robots; it is vulnerable to missing meshes and invisible steps.
Aimless exploration misses targets on other floors, and instantaneous detection causes 35% of failures (false detections); actions are discrete only.
builds_on: Ramakrishnan et al. embodied visual exploration benchmark
